aspect: The concept, and where it came from
description: Continuous traumatic stress was developed in the 1980s by clinicians in apartheid-era South Africa who found PTSD frameworks failed people whose victimisation was ongoing rather than finished.
energy_note: A diagnosis written for a war that ended.
notes: Fully developed in assets/text/war, PTS-002. Recorded here because it is the correct frame for this population specifically.

aspect: The symptoms are adaptive, which is why treating them fails
description: Avoiding a road during a closure and not sleeping during a raid are correct responses. Evidence: once a person leaves the affected area, symptoms subside dramatically - the opposite of what a conditioned false-alarm model predicts.
energy_note: Told to relax about something still happening.

aspect: It presents as rage and exhaustion rather than fear
description: The validated instrument loads on exhaustion/detachment, rage/betrayal and fear/helplessness - not PTSD's intrusion, avoidance and arousal. Clinicians looking for flashbacks miss it.
energy_note: It comes out as fury, and gets misread.

aspect: And there is no functioning system to treat it in
description: Mental health services are the first cut and the last restored, and the clinicians are living under the same conditions as the patients.
energy_note: Your therapist heard the same explosion.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the finding that safety is the treatment
description: The continuous-traumatic-stress literature reports that once a resident leaves the affected area, symptoms subside dramatically - the opposite of what a conditioned false-alarm model predicts, and the clearest evidence that the response is an accurate reading of the environment rather than a disorder.
energy_note: The symptoms stop when the shelling does.
